newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk prosecutor says ruling party threatens state.
newsitem.headline: Turk prosecutor says ruling party threatens state.

text.p: A leading prosecutor has called on the constitutional court to outlaw Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party for threatening the secularist Turkish state, according to a charge sheet seen by Reuters on Wednesday.
"It has become clear that (Welfare) has become a focus of actions contrary to the principle of secularism in the constitution," the charge sheet read.
Prosecutor Vural Savas, the head of the republican appeals court prosecutorial office, said earlier he had demanded that the constitutional court outlaw the Islam-based Welfare.
"It has pushed our country towards a civil war atmosphere," said the charge.
Welfare has upset the secularist establishment, led by the powerful army, with plans for mild Islamist reforms since it came to office in coalition with the secularist True Path Party last June.
Their alliance narrowly survived an opposition censure motion on Tuesday.
